title: Needle-Grass
subtitle: The beautiful arctic foxes, the warm seawater, and the disgraceful needle-grass all claim their place here.

items.text: People's Square, Rayashki
The group, each harboring their own thoughts, returns toward the small town. Vila and Avgust humming out a sing-song tune.
And anxious Windsong remains silent for the journey.
Vila wheels around just as they arrive at the outskirts, keeping up the cadence of the song.

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: We're here.

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: Thank you for taking care of our little Comrade Avgust, miss.

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: You mean I'm not here to be questioned? Or arrested?

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: *chuckles* Of course not.

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: Perhaps we are a little too optimistic, but when we meet a stranger, we prefer to welcome them.
Vila looks over the awkward figure, reading the expression on her face. The researcher breaks the silence with a stumble.

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: Oh, well, I'm Windsong.

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: That's a very unique name. And where is it you come from?

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: From the east side of the Dniester River.
Vila's scales are hit with a sea breeze. It halts her and their conversation.

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: *sniffs*
The teacher breaks out from her pause.

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: No offense, Ms. But you have a complicated and unfamiliar scent about you.

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: The smell of hard rocks, a lighthouse by the sea, rainwater in a humid summer. Mm. Nothing hostile, though.

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: *chuckles* I think most rootless travelers like me smell like that.

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: Welcome to Rayashki, Ms. Windsong.
Vila motions inward to the town.

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: Thank you.

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: I understand your caution. But ...
Windsong is seized by her own suspicion, spying the unusual scales on her host's neck.
Vila catches the glance. She subtly tugs at her sleeve and shrinks her neck into her coat, taking a few cautious steps backward.

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: You have nothing to worry about; it's not a disease.

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: Anyway, let's talk about you. I heard that you're a researcher.

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: Not long ago, many of your peers visited here. They wandered around and looked under every rock and floorboard in the town, like you do. I thought perhaps they were attracted here by the town itself.

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: But regrettably, not long after, they left one after another in disappointment.

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: I was disappointed, too.
There is a curiousness in her tone.

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: Will you be like them?

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: Haha.

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: Those people are famous scholars; of course, they won't spend too much time on a project with unclear prospects. But I, I'm used to those.
She spreads her hands out to the town, with nothing more to say.

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: I salute you for your courage and spirit of exploration.

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: I thought you ... I thought you might be more hostile to me. Shouting things like "Who do you think you are to prowl about on our private property!"

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: Many see the study of ley lines like finding a needle in the grass of a Siberian field—wasted effort with negligible results.

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: There's no such thing as meaningless work.

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: It doesn't matter who you are, where you're from, or what you do. You will find your purpose here.
Vila shifts her gaze over to Avgust, who has been found and surrounded by the other children not far away.

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: Is that so? No wonder how you have such an unusual student like Avgust.

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: All that childhood wonder, innocence—somehow you've preserved it in him, haven't you?
The children seem unconcerned with the new adult; they have their own world and their own rules to be addressed.

items.speaker: Avgust
items.text: Is the show finished?

items.speaker: Nina
items.text: We cancelled our rehearsal, Avgust. Mr. Evgeni just left red-faced.

items.speaker: Pyotr
items.text: Yes! And he canceled the "Friendship" cheese on the food menu, all thanks to you.

items.speaker: Avgust
items.text: But I was welcoming our new friend!

items.speaker: Pyotr
items.text: And we have lost our cheese because of you. This is all your fault!

items.speaker: Pyotr
items.text: You're the most bothersome kid in Rayashki!

items.speaker: Avgust
items.text: I know that word! "Most" means the best! So thank you, Pyotr.

items.speaker: Pyotr
items.text: You!
The other children gather close.

items.speaker: Pasono
items.text: Avgust, we don't see anyone new here. You're not lying again, are you?

items.speaker: Avgust
items.text: She's with Vila! They greet each other, share footprints, and even sing together.

items.speaker: Avgust
items.text: Windsong is also the "best"! She can draw many lines on the snow, and even on a seagull.

items.speaker: Pyotr
items.text: We're not having another freak in town, right?

items.speaker: Nina
items.text: Do you mean drawing on the blackboard? Like Ms. Vila did?
Avgust playfully shakes his head, feigning an air of mystery.

items.speaker: Avgust
items.text: She made the earth turn into a tall tall wall, and she blew her breath at it, and made a building appear.

items.speaker: Avgust
items.text: If we had enough ley hunters like her working together, we would be able to send sunflowers high into the sky!

items.speaker: Pyotr
items.text: Ah, that's not so tough! All the men in town know how to build stuff like that!

items.speaker: Pyotr
items.text: When we grow up, we will work like them, with hoes and shovels.

items.speaker: Pasono
items.text: But that will take ages.

items.speaker: Nina
items.text: If we can learn how to build like the ley hunters, then we could help the adults right now!

items.speaker: Pyotr
items.text: Don't listen to Avgust!
The children discuss the notion animatedly. Pyotr finds himself squeezed out of their huddle.
He puffs his cheeks and hurries over to the adults.

items.speaker: Pyotr
items.text: Greetings, Ms. Windsong.

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: Mm?

items.speaker: Pyotr
items.text: Is it true? Can you really shape the earth into different things and build things from it?

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: Not exactly. The things I build with my arcane skill have only a momentary effect. I can't use it that way. I learned it as a part of my research while studying ley lines.
The other children join in.

items.speaker: Nina
items.text: Ms. Windsong, those things Avgust told us, are they true?

items.speaker: Nina
items.text: The sun that closes its eyes, the dark clouds that spit on people, and the lines that can reveal everything.

items.speaker: Pasono
items.text: Ms. Windsong, will you be our teacher, like Ms. Vila?

items.speaker: Pyotr
items.text: Can you prove anything?

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: Kids. One question at a time.
The children surround Windsong, catching her off guard.
She looks apologetically at Vila.

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: Sorry, Ms. Vila. I should explain it to them.

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: Mine is not a ... formal discipline. Many people believe that it "relies too much on the observations of arcanists" and "the conclusions aren't useful for the public."

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: So it is best that you kids do not study it.
She shrugs her shoulders.

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: A pursuit of passion, fit for only a very stubborn fool like me.

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: I see.
Vila nods in understanding.

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: Then, you must show us all about it. Shouldn't she, kids?

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: I'm sure Ms. Windsong would be very happy to give us a special lesson about her studies.

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: Huh?!

items.speaker: Avgust
items.text: Yay!
Escaping this unasked-for obligation may prove more difficult than expected.

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: Ms. Vila! I thought I made myself clear!

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: You have worked hard in this "pursuit of passion," haven't you?

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: Regardless, the study of ley lines is ... Well, it's useless.
Windsong lightly taps her yellowed notebook filled with cryptic scribbles and notes.

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: Useless?

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: These kids should learn something like geography. It's a much more thorough and important field.

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: As far as the general public and academic institutions are concerned, the study of ley lines is just a niche aspect of geography, worse still, one that is solely accessible to arcanists.

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: To devote any real time to its investigation would take up valuable research funds and equally valuable researchers.

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: At least that was how they felt about it.
Vila furrows her brow.

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: Who can say for certain?

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: What about you? Do you also think that the study of ley lines is a waste of funds and manpower?

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: I, of course, I don't. Through ley lines, we can detect arcanum-related events in the area, learn about local arcane creatures, and find the secrets hidden both above and below the earth's surface.

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: But, I can't yet prove this to people.
Vila places her hand on Windsong's shoulder.

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: Well, you don't have to prove it alone.

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: It doesn't matter what others think of your work. The only important thing is finding its uses.

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: At first, Rayashki was just a remote village far north in the Arctic Circle. People came here to share a dream of a better future. It was only by luck that we found the runium.

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: Then Zeno approached us and became our business partner.

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: For over 60 years, people here have worked together to make it what it is now.

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: We built the school, the swimming pool, and the cinema ... For everyone.

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: Rayashki embraces and takes in every newcomer. You and your studies are no exception.

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: This is where our paths meet.
Vila smiles warmly. It hits like a warm sea breeze.
A pair of hands, concealing sharp scales, extends toward Windsong.

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: Please know that ...

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: I'm not just doing this for you. I'm doing this for a better future.
Vila glances at the children not far away. Some of them seem to be solemnly saluting a sunflower, as if it were a security team guard.

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: A well-rounded education is vital in bringing up the next generation of scientists and workers.

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: Our children should learn more about this world, even from those perspectives and types of knowledge that aren't widely accepted.
Windsong looks out to them and meets the face of her unexpected friend. He waves back excitedly.

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: Thank you, Ms. Vila.
She clasps her hand; it is colder than expected, but welcoming.
